scope: Independent CPU-only audit of the completed BF16 original-versus-RegMean static next-action probe. The precision amendment is explicitly excluded.

RAN: Parsed and paired all 51 original and 51 BF16 candidate records.
Validated all 96 structured GUI records independently against the live imported canonical SCHEMA.
Recomputed every answer, valid-nonanswer, invalid, error and truncation count.
Checked all 16 candidate healthy tool calls, all four changed-tool pairs, one stable output from each of the four fs+/fs- contexts, and all three text controls.
PASSED: Exact pairing, settings, seeds, schema hash, canonical probe hash and vLLM version.
Zero invalid, error or truncated BF16 candidate records.
All healthy actions remained coherent valid nonanswers.
All three text controls were exact matches to original.
CORRECT: compare.py keys records by context, step and seed, checks plan equivalence, and computes the reported BF16 counts and gates correctly.
regmean_comparison.json matches the independent recount and correctly reports quantitative gate failure.
NOT_RUN: No inference or server process was launched by this audit.
No sampled GUI action was executed.
No OSWorld outcome or reserve/test evaluation was run.
The precision arm was not inspected or evaluated.

task_cluster_results.caveat: Each stratum contains only two tasks. The apparent fs+ effect occurs entirely on one task, so the task-level evidence is weak.

healthy_findings: Chrome: seven seeds clicked the three-dot menu and one first closed an update popup; all are coherent first steps.
LibreOffice Impress: all eight seeds clicked the File menu to begin PNG export; all are coherent first steps.
changed_tool_findings: Two fs+ samples changed from answer to a plausible continuation on the same multi-app task: one opened a terminal and one scrolled for more tutorial detail.
One additional fs+ sample remained nonanswer but changed from hotkey to scroll, so it does not contribute to the answer-rate reduction.
One true-finish sample changed from answer to a plausible but unnecessary click on an email-recipient suggestion, producing the measured 6.25-point preservation loss.
qualitative_review.corruption_assessment: No malformed, incoherent, truncated, empty or obviously corrupted output was found in the reviewed BF16 sample. The failure is insufficient selective efficacy, not output corruption.

conclusion: The BF16 centered RegMean checkpoint is healthy on this static probe but fails its predeclared primary efficacy gate: fs+ answer rate falls by only 12.5 percentage points, below the required 25 points. No OSWorld success claim follows from these regenerated next actions.
